targetVerdict.target: ≥20% query-count reduction on ≥1 flow, OR ≥50% improvement on the slowest query, with before/after EXPLAIN ANALYZE
clearingEvidence: List issues (one of the 5 required userFlows): steady-state 17 → 13 queries, -23.5%, reproducible in 3 of 4 samples across 2 independent full harness runs.

Slowest-query route: baseline's #1 slowest statement overall (UPDATE sessions SET last_activity, max 4.764ms, 121 executions across the capture) is reduced to max 0.614ms (-87.1%) and 14 executions across an equivalent 3-run capture — DB-2's throttle working exactly as designed, confirmed structurally via EXPLAIN (isolated execution 0.178ms at baseline, matching the new steady-state closely, meaning the 4.764ms was row-lock/WAL contention from concurrent duplicate writes that no longer happens).

Bonus flow Load week dashboard (not required, but the flow baseline itself added to confirm DB-4 at the SQL layer): steady-state 42 → 13 queries, -69.0%, and N+1 flips from YES to NO — the clearest single confirmation of DB-4 in this report.
contradictingExpectation: The task brief's expectation framed 'the dashboard/main-page flow' as one thing, citing '30→6 queries' for DB-4. These are two different flows in this methodology: 'Load main page' navigates to '/' which redirects to /my-week (confirmed unchanged since baseline commit 076a183), NOT /dashboard. DB-4's fix (web/src/pages/Dashboard.tsx) only touches /dashboard, which is the separate 'Load week dashboard' flow — not one of the 5 required userFlows. 'Load main page' itself only benefits from DB-2 and misses the 20% bar (-19.2%, both cold and steady). The '30→6' figure does not match this report's or baseline's own numbers for either flow and was not independently reproduced; it likely comes from a different (endpoint-level, not full-flow) measurement referenced in memory-bank/activeContext.md.

Q1 (/api/issues list, DB-5): row width dropped -67.3% (1023→335) as expected, but raw Planning/Execution ms did NOT improve — compare's 3-run steady average (2.15ms planning / 0.81ms execution) is nominally higher than baseline's reported 3-run average (~1.76ms / ~0.53ms). DB-5's evidence is payload/width, not latency — consistent with baseline's own framing of this fix as 'payload evidence, not query-count' — but the raw ms numbers should not be read as an execution-time win.

Q3 (association batch, DB-8) at baseline's own full-254-id scale: Planning Time got WORSE, +143.6% (0.753ms → 1.834ms), because parsing a literal 254-row VALUES list costs more than a single array parameter. Execution time and estimate accuracy both improved (-22.8% execution; estimate error 28.3x-under → 1.11x-under). At the realistic page size the production code actually uses (20 ids, per the PR's own stated measurement), both Planning (0.648ms) and Execution (0.301ms) are cheap in absolute terms — the planning-time regression is specific to an unrealistically large single batch.

The overall slowest statement in the compare capture is no longer the session UPDATE (now fast and rare) but /api/documents' unfiltered list query (Q2), which is NOT nominally faster than baseline (3.193ms baseline max vs 3.585-5.165ms across 3 compare runs) — untouched by any merged fix, sorts by position/created_at rather than the column DB-10's new index covers (updated_at DESC), so no regression is claimed, but no improvement either.
